status_summary: Executive Order 14182, signed 2025-01-24, revoked Executive Orders 14076 and 14079 of 2022, the orders on access to reproductive healthcare services. The HHS strategic plan page, read on 2026-10-18, still presents the 2022 to 2026 plan with an updated plan described as forthcoming and no conception-to-natural-death language. No source read confirms that the HHS task force was disbanded, that a pro-life task force was installed, or that a Special Representative for Domestic Women's Health was created.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14182 (Enforcing the Hyde Amendment) revoked Executive Orders 14076 and 14079, the 2022 orders on reproductive healthcare access.

title: Replace HHS reproductive access task force with a pro-life task force and mission language
uncertainties: Executive Order 14182 was re-read on federalregister.gov in review: signed 2025-01-24 (90 FR 8751), Sec. 2 revokes Executive Orders 14076 and 14079 and the order does not mention HHS, a task force or a strategic plan. The HHS strategic plan page on hhs.gov is labeled 2022 to 2026 with an updated plan described as forthcoming and contains no conception-to-natural-death language. Federal Register API searches since 2025-01-20 for the task force name and, in review, for HHS documents mentioning a pro-life task force returned zero documents. Internal HHS task force records, staff pages and any women's health representative appointment would not appear in these sources, so the record rests on absence of evidence; the Unified Agenda, Congress and news checks of a full systematic review were not run. Revoking the underlying orders is not confirmation that an HHS-level task force was eliminated.
